extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, corporate communicators, and students of strategic communication
extracted.subtask_description: Case-study–based guidance for designing and evaluating organizational crisis communication strategies when a crisis originates or spreads via social media. Emphasizes principles, best practices, platform choice, monitoring, timing, and integration of social media into crisis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Arthur W. Page Society principles: be honest, open and candid about the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple competing 'truths' may exist (customers, company, employees, media). Telling the truth may require taking responsibility, which can create legal exposure; mitigate by collaborating with credible sources and partnering with publics to observe and interpret events. Anti-pattern: pretending ignorance or withholding facts until compelled; example: Domino’s needed to balance honesty with legal risks and public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove it with action
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle that organizations should substantiate statements with tangible actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions can include prosecution of wrongdoers, policy or procedural changes, visible corrective steps, and using social media to demonstrate follow-through. Example: Domino’s used the CEO apology video and announced actions to show the company was acting, which helped regain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to the customer
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle: actively listen to publics and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor social media channels (tweets, blogs, forums) to surface stakeholder concerns, use listening to speed or shape responses, and incorporate public feedback into strategy. Domino’s sped up its social media plan after listening to Twitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage for tomorrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle emphasizing long-term reputation and preparedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis responses should consider future reputation impacts and organizational learning. Example: Domino’s learned to treat online crises as requiring online solutions and adapted its processes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct public relations as if the whole company depends on it
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle stressing that PR actions should reflect organization-wide responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate across functions (security, legal, senior management) and treat communications as enterprise-level, not siloed marketing. Guidance from Domino’s: involve internal teams and authorities early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realize a company's true character is expressed by its people
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle that employees’ behavior reflects organizational character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies, hiring, training, and enforcement matter; employee misconduct can trigger crises and influence response framing (e.g., labeling acts as 'rogue employees').

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain calm, patient and good-humored
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthur W. Page principle advising tone and demeanor for communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain composure publicly and internally; avoid reactive, emotional responses. Accept uncertainty and ambiguity as part of crisis dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process approaches and policy development
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger (2006) best practice: develop processes and policies for crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have documented policies that include social media integration, roles, and escalation procedures; policies should be living documents updated to reflect new platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-event planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice: plan ahead for potential crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop crisis plans that include social media contingencies before a crisis occurs. Domino’s had a social media plan but had not fully implemented it prior to the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice: partner with publics during crisis management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage watchdogs, advocacy groups, and community leaders to aid verification and narrative building; collaborating may reduce escalation but can slow response if overcautious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to the public's concerns and understand the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice emphasizing audience research and listening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment publics, monitor sentiment, and tailor messages to what stakeholders are actually concerned about. Use social listening tools to identify engaged users and influential boundary spanners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty, candor, and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice: be transparent and straightforward in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about what is known, unknown, and being done; avoid obfuscation which erodes trust. Balance transparency with legal/operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate and coordinate with credible sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice recommending coordination with trustworthy organizations and authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with local authorities, consumer watchdogs, and credible third parties to verify facts and amplify accurate information. Domino’s worked with GoodAsYou.org and local authorities to identify perpetrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the needs of the media and remain accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice: be available and responsive to media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely updates, media materials, and access to spokespersons. In social crises, be present on platforms where the story is unfolding rather than only traditional press channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with compassion, concern and empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice urging empathetic messaging during crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge stakeholder emotions, express concern, and articulate corrective intent. Domino’s apology video combined empathy with action announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept uncertainty and ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice: tolerate unknowns during crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admit uncertainty when appropriate, avoid premature definitive statements, and explain efforts to verify facts. Train spokespeople to handle ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messages of self-efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeger best practice advising messages that empower stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information that helps stakeholders feel they can respond or protect themselves (e.g., steps taken, resources available). Use clear calls-to-action when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate social media into risk and crisis management policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Veil, Buehner, & Palenchar recommendation to make social media engagement part of formal policies and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include social media roles, approved platforms, monitoring responsibilities, and escalation paths in crisis manuals; avoid ad-hoc decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate social media when scanning the environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Veil et al. guidance to include social media in ongoing environment scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social listening for early warning signals, rumor detection, and stakeholder sentiment tracking. Tools and human monitoring should be combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in rumor management and channel selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Veil et al. recommendation to use social media actively in rumor management and to select appropriate channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where rumors are spreading, correct misinformation promptly on the same platforms, and choose channels that target affected publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social media to communicate updates in an interpersonal manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Veil et al. suggestion to use social platforms for timely, conversational updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver updates that feel direct and human (short posts, videos, replies); monitor responses and engage where appropriate rather than pushing only broadcast statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess stakeholder attributions (Situational Crisis Communication Theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coombs' SCCT: crises trigger stakeholder attributions along three dimensions: (1) history/repeatability, (2) controllability by individual or organization, (3) internal vs external locus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how stakeholders will attribute responsibility to inform response choice; in Domino’s case, the crisis was internal (employee actions) but not organizationally intended, shaping a responsorial strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-step crisis response process
rubrics_metrics.description: Coombs-derived procedural rubric: 1) observe events; 2) interpret information for accuracy and relevance; 3) choose a strategy among alternatives; 4) implement the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cycle quickly and iteratively. Observation requires monitoring tools; interpretation requires fact-checking (legal/security input); strategy selection should align with best practices and chosen channels; implementation must be coordinated and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the response medium to the crisis medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion to use the same or preferred platforms as those where the crisis is occurring (e.g., use YouTube/Twitter if videos/tweets caused the crisis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fighting 'viral with viral' can be effective: Domino’s used YouTube to publish the CEO apology because the prank spread there. Anti-pattern: posting only on corporate webpages while conversation occurs on social sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate social media into crisis communication strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must treat social media as part of their crisis strategies, not separate marketing channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for social media in advance, include social tactics in drills, designate platform owners, and have ready-to-deploy content templates (e.g., video, short updates). Domino’s had a plan but had not fully implemented it pre-crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor social media dialogue and provide regular updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously monitor social platforms and issue regular, consistent updates across multiple channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools (HootSuite, Bottlenose) for cross-platform posting and monitoring. Regular updates address speed expectations and maintain visibility; failure to update promptly can amplify stakeholder frustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance speed of response with verification to avoid legal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond quickly in social media crises but verify facts to prevent legal exposure and misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rushed, unverified claims can create liability; Domino’s hesitated to verify, which led to a 24-hour lag and public questioning. Establish rapid verification protocols involving security and legal teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit and leverage boundary spanners / highly engaged users
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on identifying and nurturing online users with high involvement and social identity to help manage reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use influencers and engaged users to amplify accurate information and counter misinformation. Consider outreach and relationship-building pre-crisis so these actors can be allies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage online reputation through search engine optimization (SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SEO tactics to influence what stakeholders find when searching about the crisis or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create optimized content (videos, FAQs, press materials) that ranks for crisis-related searches to push down harmful user-generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine which stakeholder messages/images will tip toward a crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop criteria to identify what UGC (user-generated content) is likely to escalate into a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create triage rules (e.g., scale, graphic content, involvement of employees) to prioritize responses; monitor trending signs (shares, comments) that indicate tipping points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate internal teams and external authorities quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring together social media teams, corporate comms, legal, security, and external credible sources at the outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early internal coordination ensures consistent messaging and fact verification. Domino’s involved social media staff, security, senior management, and watchdog groups within the first 24 hours.
